# D-018 — Update DTOs and metamodels are generated, never hand-written

**Status:** accepted
**Invariant:** `vv_gen.go` is generated output; a change to it must come from re-running `cmd/vv`, and the generated file must be reproducible from the model source.

## The decision

`cmd/vv` reads a package's Go source with `go/parser`, finds the structs that
carry `db` or `rel` tags (or are named with `-types`), and writes two things per
model into `vv_gen.go`:

- `<Model>Update` — the partial-update DTO, `*T` for a non-nullable column and
  `crud.Opt[T]` for a nullable one ([[D-002]]);
- `<Model>Attrs` plus `var Model_ = specs.Metamodel[Model, ModelAttrs]()` — the
  typed metamodel, expanded through relations to `-depth` levels. Every expanded
  relation group embeds a `specs.Rel[Root, Target]`, so the relation's canonical
  *path* is an identifier too — `Article_.Comments.Path()` — and not only the
  columns on the far side of it.

With `-adapter` it writes the resource half as well: `<Model>Input`,
`<Model>Mapper`, `<Model>Paths` — the inverse of that mapping — `<Model>Service`
and `Mount<Model>`. And whether or not `-adapter` is on, the file ends in an
`init` asserting that the DTO covers every writable column ([[D-050]]).

`<Model>Input` omits a primary key explicitly marked `auto` together with generated and
lock columns. An assigned/client-owned primary key remains in the input. The
inverse path-map declaration carries that omitted key as an explicit
exclusion, so its runtime totality check agrees with the actual wire body.

The file carries `// Code generated by vv. DO NOT EDIT.` and is checked in.

## Why

**Why generated rather than reflective at run time.** The DTO could be a
`map[string]any` and the filter API could take strings. Both work and both move
the failure to a request: rename `CreatedAt` to `PublishedAt` and a hand-written
DTO still compiles, a string filter still compiles, and the break shows up as a
400 in production. Generated code breaks the build.

**Why the relation path is generated too, and not only the columns.** The same
argument, on the half that was left out. `sqlrepo.RelationScope("Comments", …)` and
a relation policy are declarations whose failure mode is worse than a 400:
rename the relation and the declaration still compiles, still reads as
protection, and narrows nothing at all. `Path()` makes that rename a build
failure at every call site. The string form stays — a path that arrives over the
wire is a string and cannot be anything else ([[UC-007]] guarantee 18).

**Why the handle carries the target model.** `Rel[M, T]` checks `T` against the
relation at package initialisation. Without it a handle could name a real path
and the predicate beside it could be written against the wrong model, which is a
narrowing applied to a table nobody meant to narrow — and the path itself would
still look right.

**Why three method names for one string.** The handle is embedded, so `Path` is
promoted at depth one while every column of the *target* is a field of the same
group at depth zero, and Go resolves the shallower one. A target with a column
called `Path` therefore shadows the method for that one relation. Embedding is
still the right shape — `Article_.Comments.Path()` is what a reader expects, and
the alternative spellings were all worse at every other call site — so the case
is handled rather than designed around: `String` is the second chance, `RelPath`
is the spelling nothing shadows, and the generator emits a note in the affected
group's doc comment so the reader finds it where they are already looking.

**Why generated rather than hand-written.** A DTO is mechanical — one field per
writable column, with the nullability rule from [[D-002]] applied. Hand-writing
it means the nullability decision is made by whoever is typing, per field, per
model, forever, and the wrong choice is silent: a `*T` where `Opt[T]` belongs
loses the ability to write NULL, and nobody notices until a client tries.

**Why an explicitly auto key is not in the entity body.** The database owns it
and the create path sanitises it already. Advertising it in generated JSON made
the wire contract promise an input that was silently erased. This is distinct
from an assigned UUID/slug key, which the client does own and the input keeps.
The generator currently requires the `auto` option to know this; runtime's
implicit integer-PK default and `noauto` opt-out are a remaining parity gap, so
this paragraph does not claim every conventionally auto `ID` is already closed.

**Why AST declarations plus export-data type information, rather than importing
the model package.** The generator runs before the DTO exists and the package
may be temporarily incomplete, so executing or importing it would make
generation depend on yesterday's output. `go/parser` remains the declaration
source. A best-effort `go/types` check with function bodies ignored classifies
resolved field types and external export data; unresolved ordinary code is
harmless, while an anonymous type that cannot be classified is refused at its
declaration.

**Why the flags exist.** Each one answers a case the default cannot.

| flag | the case |
| --- | --- |
| `-types User,Article` | ent's generated entities carry no `db` tags and do not live in vv's `model.go` / `*.model.go` / `*_model.go` convention. Naming them explicitly is what makes those foreign structs models. |
| `-import` + `-into` | write the output into *your* package instead of the ORM's. `UserUpdate` would collide with ent's own update builder, and `ent generate` owns that directory and would delete or overwrite the file. `-into` without `-import` is refused, because the generated file could then not name the model types. The parsed package declaration is the preferred qualifier; a reserved/colliding name receives a readable path-derived alias. |
| `-readonly CreatedAt` | a server-owned column: still filterable, sortable and present in the metamodel, but out of the update DTO. It was described here as *the same effect as `db:",immutable"` for a struct you do not own and cannot tag*, and that was true while the DTO was the only artefact. Since [[D-050]] the two part company on the entity body: `immutable` is insert-only, so it belongs in a create; `-readonly` is server-owned, so it belongs in neither body. |
| a `version` / `lock` column | left out of the DTO and kept in the metamodel, without a flag. The repository advances the lock, and `crud.PlanFor` refuses a DTO that names it — so this is not a preference, it is the only shape that declares. |
| `-skip Internal` | drop the field entirely, like `db:"-"`. For a column the API should not know about at all — it leaves the metamodel too, so it is not filterable either. That is the difference from `-readonly` and it is the reason both exist. |
| `-depth` | relation expansion is a tree and a cyclic schema is infinite. Default 2. |
| `-no-dto` / `-no-meta` | generate one half. |
| `-adapter` | the resource has a wire shape of its own — an entity body, a mapper onto the model, and the inverse of that mapping. Generated rather than written because a hand-written inverse is wrong the first time somebody renames a key, and because generated is where totality can be demanded ([[D-050]]). Default off: turning it on rewrites the wire shape of a resource that switches to the generated wiring. |
| `-binding net` | which transport the wiring is written for. `none` writes the resource without wiring. Fiber and Gin wiring would import a satellite module, which a consumer may do and the library's own generated files may not ([[D-033]]); they wait for phase 9 alongside gRPC. |

**Why embedded structs are flattened.** The runtime flattens them
(`crud/meta.go:collectFields`), so the generator has to as well or `gorm.Model`
would silently take `ID` and the timestamps out of the metamodel — the fields
would exist at run time and be missing at compile time.
The exact boundary is: a completely untagged anonymous non-scalar value struct
is flattened. `time.Time`, driver `Valuer`/`Scanner` and text marshal/unmarshal
method-set shapes follow the exact runtime receiver rules, including scalar
pointers. An explicit `db` or `rel` tag belongs to the anonymous field and
prevents flattening. `rel:""` retains tag presence and runtime inference;
relation targets follow local aliases to their canonical model. Scalar
non-`-` relations are refused, while scalar `rel:"-"` remains a column. Local aliases,
instantiated generics and exported external bases are read through `go/types`;
`gorm.Model` keeps its audited semantic override. Any still-unresolved
anonymous type is a generation-time refusal, not an empty flattening result.
So is an external exported field whose private type the output package cannot
spell, including anonymous arrays, maps and interfaces whose unexported member
identity belongs to another package. `db:"-"` is the deliberate whole-field
escape. Untagged pointers to non-scalar embedded structs are refused in the
same pass, matching runtime metadata. Flattened effective Go names and database
columns are checked for duplicates before rendering; runtime refuses the same
schema and generated structs cannot spell duplicate fields.

**Why a struct-typed field from the same package is skipped.** It is a relation
holder or somebody else's bookkeeping, never a column. That is what keeps ent's
`Edges UserEdges` out of the DTO, and it mirrors the runtime rule.

**Why generated import ownership is explicit.** Import-path basenames
are not package names: `/v2` commonly declares the same name as v1, and source
files may rename an import. Two files may also use one local alias for two
different paths. `prepareImports` reads the source qualifier (and the declared
name for an unaliased version path), assigns aliases after sorting paths, and
rewrites each field type through its own file's map in one AST pass. Collisions
use readable path-derived aliases (`alphaCommon`, `betaCommon`), never numeric
fallbacks. The renderer walks every surviving package selector in composite
and generic types, ignores selector roots bound to generated locals, and
deduplicates by import path. Canonical default packages may retain bare imports;
every non-canonical assignment is explicit. Dot imports and same-package source
aliases that collide with an authored or generated package declaration are
refused before write, because no output-only rewrite can make those source files
legal. `-into` checks destination declarations and file import aliases in both
directions, and final rendered support imports are validated before any write.

## What it forbids

- Do not hand-edit `vv_gen.go`. The `DO NOT EDIT` header is not decorative;
  `TestGeneratedFileIsUpToDate` and `TestTheGeneratedStoresAreUpToDate`
  regenerate and compare.
- Do not make the generator's output depend on map iteration order. See
  [[D-014]] — model names and imports are sorted, and the up-to-date tests only
  work because of it.
- Do not merge `-skip` and `-readonly` into one flag. They differ in whether the
  field survives in the metamodel, which is the difference between "not
  writable" and "not addressable".
- Do not write into the ORM's own directory. `-into` exists because that
  directory is owned by the ORM's generator.
- Do not add a field to a generated DTO by hand instead of tagging the model.
- Do not hand-write or hand-edit the inverse path map. It is generated with the
  mapping it inverts, and the start-up check is what enforces that ([[D-050]]).
- Do not rename or remove `Rel.Path`, `Rel.RelPath` or `Rel.String`. They answer
  one string on purpose: two of them exist only because the third can be shadowed
  by a column of the target model, and dropping either escape leaves that
  relation with no typed spelling at all.
- Do not drop the exclusion list the generated file carries. `-skip` and
  `-readonly` are invisible to reflection, so those literals are the only thing
  that carries a flag into a file the runtime reads. A `-skip`ped column's name
  therefore appears in the generated file exactly once, and that is not the same
  as the field surviving.

## Where it lives

- `cmd/vv/main.go` — the flags, and the package doc that lists every one with
  its reason. Nothing else: the generator is `internal/codegen`, so it can be
  tested without a command line.
- `internal/codegen/codegen.go:generator.load` — parses the directory, two
  passes: struct names first so a field whose type is a local struct is
  recognised as a relation holder rather than a column.
- `internal/codegen/codegen.go:generator.parseModel` — tag reading, the `-types`
  override, the skip rules.
- `internal/codegen/types.go` — module-aware export-data loading, scalar and
  relation classification, alias/generic flattening and inaccessible-type
  refusal.
- `internal/codegen/codegen.go:generator.exclude` and `field.tagDropped` — which
  of the two reasons a column left, and therefore whether the generated file has
  to declare it.
- `internal/codegen/codegen.go:dtoType` — the `*T` / `crud.Opt[T]` decision.
- `internal/codegen/codegen.go:attrType` — `Str` / `Ord` / `Cmp` / `Attr`.
- `crud/decorators/specs/metamodel.go:Rel` — the relation handle, its three
  accessors and the reason there are three.
- `crud/decorators/specs/metamodel.go:bindRel` — the two refusals: a handle at
  the root, and a handle whose declared target is not where the relation lands.
- `crud/decorators/specs/metamodel.go:relType` — what separates the handle from
  a group that merely embeds one. Embedding promotes the setters, so without it
  the root metamodel reads its first relation group as a misplaced handle.
- `internal/codegen/codegen.go:wellKnownEmbeds` — the audited `gorm.Model`
  semantic override.
- `internal/codegen/types.go:generator.flattenType` — local and external
  resolvable bases, instantiated generics, and deterministic refusal for the
  unsafe boundary.
- `internal/codegen/render.go:generator.render` — the output, including the sorted
  import block.
- `internal/codegen/render.go:generator.renderAttrs` — relation expansion with the
  depth bound and a cycle guard.
- `internal/codegen/adapter.go` — the `-adapter` half and the coverage assertion.
- `scripts/modules.sh:generate` — regenerates the library's own examples and all three test
  stores. A store added without a line here is silently never regenerated.
- `_examples/example/blog/vv_gen.go`, `test/entstore/vv_gen.go`,
  `test/gormstore/vv_gen.go`, `test/versionstore/vv_gen.go` — the checked-in
  outputs.

## Proven by

- `TestGeneratedFileIsUpToDate` in `_examples/example/blog/blog_test.go` and
  `TestTheGeneratedStoresAreUpToDate` in `test/codegen/codegen_test.go` —
  regenerate and diff, both in the unit suite and neither needing a database.
  These are what make the checked-in files trustworthy, and each checks the
  `//go:generate` line verbatim so the test and the tree cannot drift apart.
- `TestAGeneratedResourceRefusesToStartWhenAColumnIsMissing` in
  `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go` — the half regenerate-and-diff cannot
  reach, because that comparison only measures the generator against itself
  ([[D-050]]).
- `TestTheGeneratedMapCoversEveryWritableColumn` and
  `TestTheGeneratedAssertionNamesTheReadonlyExclusions` in
  `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go` — the `-adapter` half and the exclusion
  list, each with its control.
- `TestAnAssignedPrimaryKeyRemainsInTheGeneratedInput` — only database-owned
  keys disappear; an assigned key remains a request field.
- `TestAVersionedModelGeneratesAResourceThatStarts` in
  `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go` and the three tests in
  `test/versionstore/versionstore_test.go` — the version case, which had no
  model in the tree to notice it with.
- `TestGeneratedCodeCompilesAndValidates` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go` — the
  output is not just text; it compiles and the resulting DTO validates against
  the model's schema.
- `TestOutputIsByteIdenticalAcrossRuns` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go`.
- `TestRelationGroupsCarryATypedPath` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go` —
  with the root as its control, since the root is reached through no relation and
  must not be handed a path.
- `TestATargetColumnNamedPathIsCalledOut` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go` —
  the shadowing case is announced where the group is declared, with the other
  direction of the same schema as the control.
- `TestARelationHandleAnswersItsCanonicalPath`,
  `TestARelationHandleDeclaringTheWrongTargetIsRefused` and
  `TestARelationHandleAtTheRootIsRefused` in
  `crud/decorators/specs/edge_test.go` — the group is declared under a Go field
  name that is *not* the relation's, so the path can only have come from binding.
- `TestARelationScopeAcceptsAGeneratedPath` in `crud/sqlrepo/relscope_test.go` —
  the other end of the seam, with the literal spelling of the same declaration as
  the control that the two render the identical statement.
- `TestGeneratedDTOTypesFollowNullability` in `_examples/example/blog/blog_test.go` and
  `TestUpdateDTOFollowsNullability` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go`.
- `TestUpdateDTOLeavesOutWhatCannotBeWritten` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go`.
- `TestReadonlyKeepsAFieldQueryableButNotWritable` and
  `TestSkipRemovesAFieldEverywhere` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go` — the pair that
  pins the difference between the two flags. The `-readonly` test asserts the
  field is *still in the metamodel*, which is the half that would otherwise rot.
- `TestIntoAnotherPackageQualifiesTheModelTypes`,
  `TestIntoAnExistingPackageKeepsItsName` and `TestIntoWithoutImportIsRefused` in
  `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go`.
- `TestEmbeddedStructsAreFlattened` and
  `TestGormModelIsFlattenedFromTheWellKnownTable` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go`.
- `TestAnonymousTypeClassificationMatchesRuntimeAndGeneratedPackageCompiles`
  and `TestExternalEmbedWithAnInaccessibleColumnTypeFailsAtGeneration` — the
  runtime/codegen classification matrix, empty-tag/alias relation expansion,
  structural accessibility and the fail-loud edge.
- `TestReadableCollisionAliasesCompile`,
  `TestSourceImportAliasCollidingWithGeneratedDeclarationIsRefused`, and
  `TestIntoDestinationImportAliasCollidingWithGeneratedDeclarationIsRefused`
  — readable imports where rewriting is possible and bidirectional refusal
  where Go cannot represent the result.
- `TestConcatenatedRelationDeclarationCollisionIsRefused` — relation-derived
  declaration collisions refuse before write.
- `TestRelationsBecomeNestedAttributeStructs` and
  `TestDepthBoundsHowFarRelationsExpand` in `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go`.
- `TestGeneratingOnlyOneHalf` and `TestAPackageWithoutModelFilesIsAnError` in
  `internal/codegen/codegen_test.go`.
- `TestEntGeneratedMetamodel` in `test/integration/ent_model_test.go` — the
  `-types` case against ent's real generated entity.
